Their prerequisites therefore contain standard-enabled rather than signed-enabled; disabled_features does not add a missing signed prerequisite. Both rows select feature_disabled false, missing_prerequisites [], and status runtime-unrun.

findings.evidence: validate_manifest in lab/storage_write_settlement.py lines 169 through 184 allows unique writers in any order. DockerLocalCommands.containers at line 370 passes sorted(ids) to inspect. decode_inventory iterates containers_before at line 142 and appends each writer at line 198 without restoring manifest order. stopped_observation at lines 229 through 234 uses zip with the manifest list and requires positional CID equality. LocalNativeAuthority.reconcile at line 683 and DockerLocalCommands.storage_rows at line 460 invoke this validator, so a valid enrolled multiwriter set can stop successfully yet cannot perform file/row capture. The approved 142 Python, 3 hybrid and 78 Bun checks all pass; native authority tests construct a one-writer candidate and do not cover the reversed two-writer parser composition. No native admission bypass or actual service failure is claimed.
findings.location: stopped_observation, lines 229 through 234; decode_inventory, lines 142 and 198; DockerLocalCommands.containers, line 370
findings.reproduction: Static counterexample, not an executed additional probe: enroll two otherwise valid writers in manifest order [b repeated 64 times, a repeated 64 times], with their matching process/configuration entries and both observed cleanly stopped. Supply identical before/after Docker inventories in sorted CID order, as DockerLocalCommands.containers constructs them. decode_inventory accepts the exact set and returns writers in [a, b] order. stopped_observation compares that list positionally against [b, a] and raises 'Every original writer must be observed stopped before capture'.
findings.requested_change: Normalize decoded writer observations to the manifest order, or validate the complete unique stopped set by CID while preserving exact identity checks. Add a private source regression that composes decode_inventory with stopped_observation for a reverse-ordered two-writer manifest and sorted Docker observations, retaining missing/duplicate/foreign/running-writer refusals.

findings.evidence: The signed SDK helpers perform createSignedUploadUrl/uploadToSignedUrl and createSignedUrl/fetchSigned at drill lines 70 through 85. storage_write_settlement.py line 26 declares signed separately from standard, and line 187 requires both feature flags. The existing disabled-feature regression at test_disposable_storage_settlement_drill.py lines 103 through 115 covers tus, queue, redis, and remote_s3 but omits signed. This contradicts the NS1 requirement to report each case's missing real prerequisites. findings.recommended_change: Bind signed-enabled to both signed SDK cases, make disabled signed ingress force prerequisite-unavailable for those rows, and add a frozen discriminating source regression. Keep standard-enabled where ordinary SDK behavior is also required. Preserve native_accepted false.
findings.reproduction: Static branch evaluation, not an executed additional probe: collect the declared prerequisite strings from case_matrix(), supply all of them as available_prerequisites, and call case_matrix(available_prerequisites, ['signed']). The sdk-signed-upload and sdk-signed-download IDs fall through the feature selection to standard. Their prerequisites therefore contain standard-enabled rather than signed-enabled; disabled_features does not add a missing signed prerequisite. Both rows select feature_disabled false, missing_prerequisites [], and status runtime-unrun.

findings.evidence: validate_manifest in lab/storage_write_settlement.py lines 169 through 184 allows unique writers in any order. DockerLocalCommands.containers at line 370 passes sorted(ids) to inspect. decode_inventory iterates containers_before at line 142 and appends each writer at line 198 without restoring manifest order. stopped_observation at lines 229 through 234 uses zip with the manifest list and requires positional CID equality. LocalNativeAuthority.reconcile at line 683 and DockerLocalCommands.storage_rows at line 460 invoke this validator, so a valid enrolled multiwriter set can stop successfully yet cannot perform file/row capture. The approved 142 Python, 3 hybrid and 78 Bun checks all pass; native authority tests construct a one-writer candidate and do not cover the reversed two-writer parser composition. No native admission bypass or actual service failure is claimed.

findings.reproduction: Static counterexample, not an executed additional probe: enroll two otherwise valid writers in manifest order [b repeated 64 times, a repeated 64 times], with their matching process/configuration entries and both observed cleanly stopped. Supply identical before/after Docker inventories in sorted CID order, as DockerLocalCommands.containers constructs them. decode_inventory accepts the exact set and returns writers in [a, b] order. stopped_observation compares that list positionally against [b, a] and raises 'Every original writer must be observed stopped before capture'.
findings.requested_change: Normalize decoded writer observations to the manifest order, or validate the complete unique stopped set by CID while preserving exact identity checks. Add a private source regression that composes decode_inventory with stopped_observation for a reverse-ordered two-writer manifest and sorted Docker observations, retaining missing/duplicate/foreign/running-writer refusals.

findings.evidence: The loop condition at line 33 depends only on open output pipes. The unguarded wait at line 55 precedes cleanup at lines 56 through 57 and cumulative accounting at lines 59 through 61. No try/finally encloses the launched process. RLIMIT_CPU does not bound sleeping wall time. A child in the new session created at line 26 can therefore remain alive while its elapsed time is absent from the shared 180-second ledger. The three approved checks passed normally and did not exercise this exceptional path.
findings.reproduction: Static trigger, not executed: an owned test process closes stdout and stderr, then continues running longer than three seconds. Both selector registrations disappear, so the monitoring loop ends even though the process remains alive. proc.wait(timeout=3) raises TimeoutExpired before the following group kill and budget persistence.
findings.requested_change: Keep supervising until process termination as well as pipe closure. Place owned group termination, bounded reaping and cumulative budget persistence in unconditional cleanup, including timeout and interruption paths. Freeze any discriminating runner reproduction before execution.
findings.title: Pipe closure bypasses supervision and exception cleanup

findings.evidence: Line 45 checks the old size before reads. Lines 50 and 52 read up to 65536 bytes per ready stream and append every byte without limiting retention to the remaining cumulative allowance. Line 58 joins and writes all retained chunks. Child RLIMIT_FSIZE at line 28 does not cap pipe output or the supervisor's log write. Thus a failure is detected, but the declared 16 MiB combined captured-output ceiling is not enforced. Actual approved outputs remained below the cap, with final cumulative output 397293 bytes.
findings.reproduction: Static trigger, not executed: the previous role output plus current captured output approaches 16777216 bytes, then either output pipe delivers another chunk. The full chunk is retained and can cross the cap. The next loop detects the excess but continues retaining queued pipe data after killing the group.
findings.requested_change: Track observed output separately from retained output, retain only the remaining cumulative allowance, kill immediately on crossing it, and discard subsequent drained bytes while preserving an explicit failure reason. Freeze any discriminating output-bound reproduction before execution.
findings.title: The cumulative retained-output cap is exceeded before refusal
